name: Question 18
worked_solution:
The integral is defined over the type I region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le x}.$ 

So, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)]_{0}^{x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,dx & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The integral is defined over the type I region D={(x,y):0≤x≤π2,0≤y≤x}.

So, we can express the integral, as follows:

∬Dsin⁡(x+y)dA=∫0π/2∫0xsin⁡(x+y)dydx

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to y, treating x as a constant:

∫0π/2∫0xsin⁡(x+y)dydx=∫0π/2[∫0xsin⁡(x+y)dy]dx=∫0π/2[−cos⁡(x+y)]0xdx=∫0π/2(−cos⁡(2x)+cos⁡x)dx

Then, we integrate with respect to x:

∫0π/2(−cos⁡(2x)+cos⁡x)dx=[−12sin⁡(2x)+sin⁡x]0π/2=−12sin⁡π+sin⁡(π2)−0=1
